docTitle: October 2026 developer security news, in plain words

slides.title: The security news every developer should know from October 2026
slides.sub: PHP2Shell, Railway, Zeabur, OpenCode, eMudhra and a hacker using AI agents, in plain words.

slides.title: Two critical holes in PHP, rated *9.2 out of 10*
slides.body: PHP runs nearly three quarters of the websites in the world, so this one touches a lot of us.

slides.title: It happens before your code *even runs*
slides.body: It happens while PHP reads the request, so authentication and middleware can't block it.

slides.title: The fix is an update and a *restart*
slides.body: Then restart PHP-FPM or Apache and rebuild your Docker images. Updating Laravel alone doesn't fix it.

slides.title: Railway asked users to *rotate their keys*
slides.body: Railway said someone may have accessed customers' encrypted environment variables.

slides.title: Zeabur is shutting down after *two breaches*
slides.body: The second used an admin token with no expiry date, unchanged since January 2024.

slides.title: Stolen AI keys, *real bills*
slides.body: Attackers took AI keys stored in OpenCode Console. Users saw charges in the hundreds, and a few went over $1,000.

slides.title: Three of them went for the *same place*
slides.lede: That's where developers keep their secret keys. These habits limit the damage.
rows: Give every key an expiry date
Give each key only what it needs

slides.title: One signing key was the *number 4*
slides.body: eMudhra issues certificates that browsers trust. Its keys were so weak that browsers have blocked them.

cols.v: One hacker used AI agents on 100+ companies.

slides.title: When did you last check *your keys*?
slides.body: I put all of these stories in one video, in plain words.
